text: There's a planet out there as blue as Earth, and its weather would kill you in seconds.
It's a gas giant about sixty-four light-years away, and its name is just a catalogue number.
From far away, it would look a lot like home. A deep, azure blue.
But that blue doesn't come from oceans.
It hugs its star so tightly that a whole year there lasts just over two days.
The side facing its star is around a thousand degrees Celsius.
Winds rip around it at about seven thousand kilometres an hour. Nearly six times the speed of sound.
And scientists think that blue may come from tiny drops of glass, floating in the air.
Glass that may fall as rain.
So the next time you complain about the weather... at least it's not raining glass.
